scope: Bound public readiness dependency work without consuming the business database pool

implementation.admission: One shared in-flight promise per process, one cached boolean for 2000 ms after completion, including failures
implementation.database: Separate max-1 PostgreSQL pool, application_name ziyatai-readiness, connection/query/server statement timeouts each 2000 ms
implementation.storage: HeadBucket uses an AbortSignal with a 2000 ms deadline
implementation.response: Only status ok or degraded; errors never include dependency details. HTTP responses remain no-store
implementation.routes: GET/HEAD only, exact root/live/ready routes; liveness has no dependency checks

verification.unit: 109 passed; 200 concurrent probe calls share one promise; success/failure cache expiry, synchronous failures, missing heartbeat, DB/storage errors and recovery tested
verification.realStorageAndDatabase: 100 concurrent anonymous HTTP readiness requests succeeded; pg_stat_activity reported exactly one dedicated readiness connection
verification.protocol: HEAD has no body; unsupported methods return 405 and Allow; unknown paths return 404
verification.chromium: Eight cases passed: readiness/protocol, session recovery and all private streaming download regressions
verification.build: Production Docker image, lint, typecheck, formatting, source visibility and recognizable-secret scan passed

limitations: Limits apply per API process; they are not a distributed global ingress or process-memory limit
The cached result may lag dependency state by up to two seconds
The DB connection and subsequent query each have their own timeout; this does not promise a single two-second response deadline
Readiness checks DB, storage and worker heartbeat; antivirus, renderer and public TLS require separate monitoring
The short burst is not a sustained load test or cloud deployment acceptance
